messages:
ashley_support: FYI support ticket from Acme (pool: dedicated-us-west-3/t42). They started seeing lots of 429/504s and end-to-end latency jumped ~10x since ~2026-03-16 09:40 UTC. Rolling escalated to eng-runtime.

oliver_runtime: Thanks — can you paste a short sample of request headers/body and the tenant/pool id? Also what model + variant are they hitting? Any recent deploys to that pool?

ashley_support: Pool id in ticket: t42. Model = open-gpt-large-1 (quantized v1). No deploys from our side in past 24h. Customer says most requests are chat completions with long context prefixes and then short continuation calls. Here's anonymized curl they gave: 
```
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxx" -H "X-Customer-ID: acme" -d '{"model":"open-gpt-large-1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"...long doc..."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions
```

maya_sre: Noted. We have an alert flood for the pool: many "inference_queue_wait_exceeded" and "batch_timeout" traces. oncall-bot shows repeated autoscale up/down events over the last hour. Could be oscillation.

oncall-bot: [ALERT] pool=t42 queue_latency_p90=820ms queue_depth=42 autoscale: scale_up->scale_down->scale_up x3 in 45m.

oliver_runtime: Oscillation + high queue depth often indicates ineffective batching or micro-bursts that prevent efficient pack by tokens. Two hypotheses: (A) request shapes (very long prefixes + small completion tokens) causing continuous-batcher to create small token-limited batches; (B) noisy tenant doing long-context runs evicting shared KV cache and causing repeated expensive prefill work.

ashley_support: Acme confirms they do a lot of long-context prepends (10k tokens) then short replies (50 tokens). They also do a back-and-forth interactive loop (many sequential calls).

oliver_runtime: Please grab a 2-min pprof/log snippet from one of the affected nodes and the batcher metrics (microbatch_count, avg_tokens_per_batch, fill_rate). Also can you repro quickly with a synthetic load? devex_lina can you help with a repro script?

devex_lina: On it. Quick repro: a loop that posts the big system message then repeated small completion calls. Script (python): 
```
for i in range(200):
  requests.post(API, json={"model":"open-gpt-large-1","messages":[sys_prompt,user_q]})
```
I saw a lot of batches of size=1 and avg_tokens_per_batch ~70.

oliver_runtime: That matches hypothesis A. When avg_tokens_per_batch << max_batch_tokens we lose throughput. What is current max_batch_tokens in pool config?

maya_sre: Config shows max_batch_tokens=4096, batch_timeout_ms=20, continuous_batcher_quantum=16. Also prefill_prefers_tokens=true.

oliver_runtime: Two immediate mitigations to test: (1) Increase batch_timeout_ms to 40-60ms so the batcher has more time to pack tokens, (2) raise continuous_batcher_quantum to 32 to prefer larger merges. We should try in canary on 1 node.

ashley_support: Before changes, customer asks for repro steps they can run to validate.

oliver_runtime: Send them this minimal repro and ask them to run from their env for 60s; collect X-Request-Id from responses. Also we've added a temporary routing policy to move acme traffic off noisy shared lane (will update). Repro curl (short): 
```
for i in {1..200}; do curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -H "X-Customer-ID: acme" -d '{"model":"open-gpt-large-1","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"<10k tokens>"},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize"}]}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions; done
```

customer_acme_inc: Running now, sending response IDs. We see the same: many 429s when our loop hits spikes, and latency jumps. Thanks for the temporary routing change — that dropped errors by ~60% in first 10m.

oliver_runtime: Good — routing change suggests noisy-tenant component. We'll still tune batcher because routing is a dampener, not a fix. Next I'll attempt canary config change on one node: batch_timeout_ms=50 and continuous_batcher_quantum=32. If that stabilizes avg_tokens_per_batch and p90 tail we'll roll more broadly.

maya_sre: Also observed KV cache churn in logs: repeated prefill timeouts ~120ms correlated with high token prefill size. Noisy long-context requests seem to be forcing expensive prefill repeatedly. I'll add a metric to track prefill_hit_rate per tenant.

oliver_runtime: Canary applied to node r-w3-12 at 09:58 UTC. Monitoring...

sre-bot: [METRIC] node=r-w3-12 avg_tokens_per_batch rose from 72 -> 380 within 2m, batch_fill_rate +28%, queue_latency_p90 down 820ms -> 240ms.

oliver_runtime: Nice. Early signs good. Plan: 1) widen batch_timeout on pool to 50ms 2) increase continuous quantum 3) enable token-prefill cache isolation for heavy tenants (short-term: routing + soft-isolate) 4) longer-term: pack-by-token-first heuristic + tenant-aware scheduler.

ashley_support: Customer notified, they're seeing improvements and will keep monitoring. They asked whether this is a billing/credits side-effect (spike -> rate-limit) — do we need to check rate limiter logic?

maya_sre: Rate limiter looked OK; 429s were coming from the serving runtime throttle (batch queue full) not billing layer. We'll keep watching.

devex_lina: Repro script with canary applied shows far fewer 429s. I'll put the test script and the sample response ids in the ticket.

customer_acme_inc: Thx team — errors dropped and latencies back to acceptable. We'll reopen if we see regression.

oliver_runtime: Follow-ups logged: RH-8473 (batcher: prefer token-packing when avg_tokens_per_batch < threshold), RH-8474 (prefill_hit_rate per-tenant metric), RH-8475 (auto-route heavy long-context tenants to isolated pools). I'll attach perf graphs and the canary timestamps to the ticket.

ashley_support: Marking as ongoing monitoring, escalation downgraded. Closing for now but will reopen if customer reports new errors. :thumbsup:
